title: Quarterly Signal Grid: prioritization matrix, experiment budget, and rollback windows for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Lena Fischer
description:
Objective: Produce an operational playbook (Signal Grid) that maps prioritized product bets for the upcoming quarter across Hosted API features and model-catalog transitions, ties each bet to explicit OKR signals, assigns experiment budgets, and defines deterministic rollback windows and canary gates.

Scope: This ticket covers planning artifacts and execution guardrails for: (1) prioritization matrix (value vs. risk vs. capacity), (2) per-initiative experiment budget and KPI thresholds, (3) canary/rollout windows and automated fallback rules, (4) OKR threading into sprint commitments and stakeholder RACI. We will not execute model swaps here — this is planning and gating only.

Why now: Recent model rotations and a missed latency regression in Q4 flagged that priority and risk signals were fragmented across teams. We need a single Signal Grid so PM, Eng, and DX can coordinate canary windows, capacity hedges, and experiment budgets to avoid cross-team surprises during model swaps and hosted API changes.

Deliverables:
- Prioritization matrix spreadsheet (value/risk/cost) with linked owner for each line item
- OKR mapping document that shows how each initiative updates objective progress metrics
- Experiment budget ledger (token-hour budget, ci/canary cadence, rollback thresholds)
- Rollout choreography playbook (canary percentages, time windows, circuit-breaker thresholds)
- One-pager for executive summarization and a Confluence page for the full playbook

Acceptance criteria:
- The prioritization matrix has owners and estimated engineering effort for >90% of listed initiatives
- Each initiative has an assigned experiment budget and explicit KPI thresholds for success/failure
- Rollout choreography includes automated fallback recipes compatible with Dedicated and Hosted modes
- Stakeholders sign off on the OKR mapping and canary windows at the roadmap review meeting
- Playbook links to at least one test dashboard and an alert runbook for regressions

Stakeholders: ["Diego Martinez - PM Lead (assignee)", "Lena Fischer - Head of Product (creator)", "Aisha Nair - Eng Manager (serving runtime)", "Samir Patel - Reliability Eng", "Mei Chen - DevEx/Docs", "Customer Success: Jordan Blake"]

Key metrics / signals to wire into decisions:
- 95th percentile token latency (ms)
- Per-token unit cost (USD)
- Model quality delta on held-out evals (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic accuracy where relevant)
- Error/safety signal rate (per 10k requests)
- Canary health score (composite)

Dependencies: ["ENG-80821","PM-47209","PM-41207"]

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Overcommitting experiment budget causing capacity pressure. Mitigation: Reserve a 20% capacity hedge and surface alerts to capacity owners before canary expansion.
- Risk: Misaligned OKR expectations between Hosted and Dedicated customers. Mitigation: Tag initiatives by customer cohort and include cohort-specific guardrails in the Signal Grid.
- Risk: Runbook not executable in Private deployments. Mitigation: Validate rollback recipes in a private VPC test cluster before adoption.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Signal+Grid+Q2-2026

- PR template for rollout playbooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821
- Dashboard (canary): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/hostedapi/canary-health
- Example incident learnings: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/HostAPI-Incident-Postmortems

Execution plan & timeline:
- 2026-02-10: Kickoff and initial brain-dump (complete)
- 2026-02-12..2026-02-16: Draft prioritization matrix and OKR mapping (owners assigned)
- 2026-02-17..2026-02-18: Engineering feasibility check and capacity hedge sizing
- 2026-02-19: Roadmap review with EMs and Reliability (prep one-pager)
- 2026-02-20: Finalize playbook and publish Confluence page

Notes on decision trade-offs:
- We prefer shorter canary windows for low-risk UI-only changes but will extend to 48–72 hours for model swaps that affect semantic output. The matrix will encode a per-initiative default window with a rationale field.
- Experiment budget is defined in token-hours to make cost impact explicit; teams may swap to dollar budgets if that aligns with finance reporting.

Cross-functional review & signoffs required: ["Head of Eng","SRE Lead","DX Lead","Legal (if dataset/customer data involved)"]
